comparison: Both evaluate the core ICAM-1 knockout and BC enlargement findings (C1-C3, C10-C12). OpenEval finds strong support from convergence of knockout, quantification, and rescue experiments. Peer reviewers agree, stating 'the strength of evidence is solid using appropriate methodology' and 'conclusions are sufficiently supported by the data.' Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address characterization of ICAM-1_KO cells showing maintained cellular functions (C6-C9). OpenEval emphasizes specificity to BC size regulation rather than general dysfunction. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the solid evidence base. Partial claim overlap (C6-C9), with OpenEval also covering C4-C5 which peer R14 addresses separately. Both SUPPORTED.

Both address basic characterization of ICAM-1_KO cells (C4-C5) showing slightly reduced proliferation but similar cell size and death rates. OpenEval integrates these with other characterization data (C6-C9) to argue against general cellular dysfunction. Peer reviewers accept these control experiments without challenge. Both SUPPORTED.

Perfect claim overlap (C13-C19) addressing BC fusion evidence. OpenEval finds multiple lines of evidence support fusion, though notes C15 suggests infrequent dynamics. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'BC dimension and shape are altered' without challenging fusion observations. Both SUPPORTED with identical claim sets.

Perfect claim overlap (C20-C25) on cytokine-induced ICAM-1 upregulation and BC loss. OpenEval emphasizes causality established by C23 showing prevention in ICAM-1_KO cells. Peer reviewers accept inflammatory regulation findings as part of well-supported conclusions. Both SUPPORTED with identical claim sets.

Perfect claim overlap (C26-C34) on myosin-II localization and regulation by ICAM-1. OpenEval highlights quantification showing reduced p-MLC and MHCIIb in ICAM-1_KO with maintained F-actin, plus rescue data. Peer reviewers accept actomyosin network regulation as 'solid using appropriate methodology.' Both SUPPORTED with identical claim sets.

Perfect claim overlap (C35-C41) on pharmacological inhibition and Rho-ROCK-actomyosin signaling. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of genetic, pharmacological, and localization data. Peer reviewers accept the mechanistic framework without challenge. Both SUPPORTED with identical claim sets.

Perfect claim overlap (C42-C54) on ICAM-1 antibody immobilization experiments. OpenEval praises the well-controlled experimental design with multiple specificity controls. Peer reviewers accept ICAM-1 signaling to actomyosin as part of the core mechanism. Both SUPPORTED with identical claim sets.

Perfect claim overlap (C55-C58) on T-cell co-culture experiments. OpenEval emphasizes physiological relevance connecting mechanistic findings to leukocyte interactions. Peer reviewers acknowledge the novel link between ICAM-1's role in polarity and immune cell adhesion. Both SUPPORTED with identical claim sets.

Perfect claim overlap (C59-C66) on EBP50 identification and characterization. OpenEval describes comprehensive characterization including BioID, colocalization, immunoprecipitation, and PDZ domain analysis. Peer reviewers accept EBP50 as ICAM-1 interactor without challenge. Both SUPPORTED with identical claim sets.

Perfect claim overlap (C67-C74) on STED microscopy showing ICAM-1-EBP50 nanodomain organization. OpenEval highlights sophisticated nanoscale spatial information and engagement-induced reorganization. Peer reviewers accept structural details supporting the mechanistic model. Both SUPPORTED with identical claim sets.

Partial claim overlap (C75-C77). OpenEval addresses ICAM-1-independent EBP50 localization but ICAM-1-modulated nanoclustering. Peer R11 covers broader EBP50 knockdown effects (C75-C84). Both find evidence SUPPORTED, with OpenEval focusing on nanodomain organization and peer review accepting the full knockdown phenotype.

Strong claim overlap (C78-C84, 70% Jaccard). OpenEval addresses EBP50 knockdown phenotype and role in ICAM-1 signaling, noting mechanistic questions remain. Peer reviewers accept EBP50 regulation of ICAM-1-mediated signaling without expressing concerns. Both SUPPORTED.

Perfect claim overlap (C85-C87) on in vivo mouse validation. OpenEval notes validation of in vitro findings but acknowledges inability to separate sinusoidal ICAM-1 and immune contributions. Peer reviewers accept mouse data as part of solid evidence base. Both SUPPORTED with identical claim sets.

Strong claim overlap (C88-C94, 64% Jaccard) on organoid characterization. OpenEval finds morphological and functional data well-support BC-like structures. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, stating 'use of organoids as a model to study bile canaliculi is still not convincing' and requesting additional markers. Major disagreement: OpenEval SUPPORTED vs Peer UNCERTAIN.

Partial claim overlap (C95-C98, 29% Jaccard) on organoid ICAM-1 localization and knockout phenotype. OpenEval finds validation in 3D model without immune confounding. Peer reviewers question organoid validity for BC studies, noting misalignment of markers and lack of enclosed spaces. OpenEval SUPPORTED vs Peer UNCERTAIN for organoid model.

Partial claim overlap (C99-C101, 43% Jaccard) on organoid cell size and blebbistatin effects. OpenEval accepts these as extending actomyosin mechanism. Peer reviewers don't specifically challenge these secondary observations despite questioning overall organoid model validity. OpenEval SUPPORTED, peer acceptance implicit in R13.

Perfect claim overlap (C102-C105) on overarching conclusions. OpenEval finds synthetic conclusions well-supported by collective evidence including nanoscale organization, leukocyte-independent signaling, BC size regulation, and inflammation connection. Peer reviewers agree conclusions are 'sufficiently supported' and describe 'useful findings on novel function of apical ICAM-1.' Both SUPPORTED with identical claim sets.
